My husband and I had to make an emergency road trip this week from Southern California to the Midwest. Because we were so rushed, we didn't do things in the traditional sense, which was great because it forced me to try new methods:

  1. If you will have access to your car the entire trip, ditch the suitcase, use small tubs instead (like the $1.50 green tubs from Ikea). One tub of clothes for each person, a tub for sundries, a tub for snacks, a tub for toys/phone chargers, etc. It's so much easier. At each motel I would just grab one set of clothes for the following day and leave the rest in the trunk. Then I would carry in two tubs (the food, and sundries), and a diaper bag. I made the kids carry their own toys. It made moving in and out of motels a breeze. Also I could find things in my sundries tub faster than in a suitcase pocket.

  2. If you are traveling with young kids, lower your daily miles expectation, and then lower them again. It took my husband three days to accept we were not going to break the transcontinental land speed record. He was so frustrated that it took us two hotel stays and three days just to get to Albuquerque. Apparently he could do that leg in one day

  3. We found our kids could only stand about 5 hours in the car each day. Now mind you that five hours was broken up into mini trips. We usually could push through three hours straight before stopping for a two or three hour break, then driving another two hours to our next hotel

  4. We were doing this on a tight budget and our goal was to get to the Midwest quickly, not sight see. We found going to public playgrounds were the best thing to do during breaks. Once we got into cold regions we switched to indoor malls with play areas and Chuck E. Cheese.

  5. The average cost of a motel was $50 a night. We mostly stuck with Travelodges, Econolodges, and Howard Johnson's. They all included breakfast which was great. I stuck with one hotel/travel app to book hotels. By the third day they were giving us deep discounts. It made it worth it.

  6. You don't need to "plan ahead" by buying a bunch of snacks and other junk beforehand. It just crowds the car anyway. There is virtually a Wal-Mart every step along the way. If we needed snacks/diapers/advil/toys/hairspray/etc we would just find the nearest Wal-Mart and only buy what we needed

  7. From start to finish we spent about $800. That includes five nights of hotels and driving in a Toyota Corolla eating fast food and only splurging at Dennys

  8. My husband became very ill, so I did all the driving. It's easy peasy ladies. I joked with my husband that I guess we knew who the first person to die on the Oregon Trail would be (he didn't find that funny)
